notes: Central EU scheme administered by the European Commission/REA with no single attached host institution. The official page states that 'Doctoral Networks implement doctoral programmes, by partnerships of universities, research institutions and infrastructures, businesses including SMEs, and other socio-economic actors from different countries across Europe and beyond' and that 'Candidates wishing to apply for PhD positions under Doctoral Networks should apply to funded Doctoral Network projects by consulting their open vacancies advertised internationally, including on the EURAXESS portal.' Applications are submitted by international consortia (at least three independent legal entities), not by individual applicants to a named department, so no supervising professor can be tied to this funding line. Supervisors exist only inside each individual funded Doctoral Network project, which varies per call and per project; verifying them would require selecting one specific project (e.g. via EURAXESS vacancies), which is outside the scope of this generic programme listing. Evidence: https://marie-sklodowska-curie-actions.ec.europa.eu/actions/doctoral-networks (fetched live, rendered successfully).

Government scholarship of the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, managed by Campus France. The official page states that the programme 'allows students from 26 European Union countries to obtain scholarships to study at the Master's level in a French institution of higher education' and that 'Applications are pre-selected by the college relations teams at the French embassies. The applications are then evaluated within the Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs by collaboration specialists from the eligible fields.' The host French institution is chosen by the applicant (eligibility requires 'Being admitted to a French higher education institution in Master's 1 or Master's 2'); the scholarship is not attached to any specific university, department or supervisor, so no supervising professor exists to identify. Published contacts on the page are programme mailbox addresses (e.g. fee.allemagne@campusfrance.org, boursiers.europe@campusfrance.org), not academic supervisors. Evidence: https://www.campusfrance.org/en/france-excellence-europa-scholarship-program (fetched live, rendered successfully).

French government scholarship run by AEFE for the Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs. The official AEFE page states that 'Les meilleurs bachelières et bacheliers non français issus d'un lycée international français peuvent bénéficier d'une bourse pour poursuivre les études supérieures en France' and that files are 'évalué par le service de coopération et d'action culturelle de l'ambassade de France dans le pays concerné. Il sera ensuite examiné par l'AEFE qui le soumettra à une commission composée de spécialistes de l'enseignement supérieur et de représentants de filières d'excellence (classes préparatoires aux grandes écoles – grandes écoles – universités)'. The selecting body is a government commission, and the host French institution is chosen per applicant (any French school or university); no university, department or supervising professor is attached to the scheme. The only named individual on the page is Claudia Scherer-Effosse, directrice générale de l'AEFE, who is the agency director (the awarding body), not a doctoral/research supervisor, and she is not tied to supervision of scholarship holders. Evidence: https://aefe.gouv.fr/fr/aefe/operateur-educatif-du-ministere-de-leurope-et-des-affaires-etrangeres/dispositif-des-bourses-france-excellence-major (fetched live, rendered successfully).

DAAD scholarship database entry for a government-funded (German Federal Foreign Office) Master's scholarship open to all academic disciplines. The official DAAD page states 'This scholarship programme offers you the opportunity to continue your academic education in Germany with a postgraduate course of study' and that funding covers 'a whole postgraduate or Master's degree programme completed at a state or state-recognised university in Germany'. The applicant selects the host university and degree programme themselves ('You yourself are responsible for ensuring your application for admission to the German university for your chosen study programme is submitted by the due date'); the listing names no university, department or supervising professor. Selection is by 'An independent selection committee consisting of specialist scientists' at DAAD, not by a host professor. Only contact published is portal@daad.de (technical hotline). Evidence: https://www2.daad.de/deutschland/stipendium/datenbank/en/21148-scholarship-database/?detail=50026200 (fetched live, rendered successfully).

DAAD EPOS is an umbrella development scholarship covering a changing list of postgraduate courses, not one attached institution. The official DAAD page states 'Individual scholarships exclusively for Postgraduate courses in Germany that are listed on the List of all Postgraduate courses with application deadlines 2027/2028' and 'Applications have only to be sent to the respective course directly! ... Applications sent to the DAAD will not be forwarded to the respective course/university.' Because the host course/university (and therefore any supervising professor) varies per selected course and per applicant, and the listing itself names no institution, no supervising professor can be attached to this scholarship entry. Evidence: https://www2.daad.de/deutschland/stipendium/datenbank/en/21148-scholarship-database/?detail=50076777 (fetched live, rendered successfully).

Alexander von Humboldt Foundation fellowship in which the applicant independently chooses an academic host, so no host professor is attached to the scheme. The official page states 'The Humboldt Research Fellowship enables you to conduct your own research at various stages of your career in collaboration with a host at a German research institution of your choice' and, in the FAQ, 'You are free to choose your own academic host. The Humboldt Foundation does not provide any direct support in finding a host.' It also advises applicants to use external host-search engines (GERiT, forschungsportal.net, GEPRIS etc.), confirming that host professors are selected by the applicant, not designated by the programme. The selection committee (60-70 researchers) evaluates applications but is not a host/supervision body. Only institutional contact published is info[at]avh.de (foundation enquiry mailbox), not a supervisor address. Evidence: https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/en/apply/sponsorship-programmes/humboldt-research-fellowship (fetched live, rendered successfully).

National agency (JASSO) short-term exchange support scheme administered at the level of Japanese schools, with no attached institution or supervisor. The official page states 'JASSO offers scholarship for qualified international students who are accepted by a Japanese university, graduate school, junior college, college of technology or professional training college ... under a student exchange agreement or other student exchange arrangement on a short-term basis from 8 days to one year between Japanese school and their home higher educational institution outside Japan' and 'Applications for the scholarship will be accepted only from Japanese school.' The specific Japanese host school (and any academic supervisor) depends entirely on each bilateral exchange agreement, which the scholarship does not specify. Evidence: https://www.jasso.go.jp/en/ryugaku/scholarship_j/ukeire.html (fetched live, rendered successfully).
